newsitem.title: SPAIN: Key Spanish poll gives opposition edge over PP.
newsitem.headline: Key Spanish poll gives opposition edge over PP.

text.p: A key Spanish poll showed Spain's opposition Socialist Workers' Party (PSOE) edging out the ruling Popular Party (PP), according to a press report on Tuesday.
The barometer of the Centro de Investigaciones Sociologicas (CIS) gave the PSOE a three-point advantage in October, according to leading Spanish daily El Pais.
It showed a voting projection of 39 points for the PSOE compared to 36 for the PP, with direct voting intentions at 27 and 21 points, respectively.
The Popular Party threw the Socialists out of government last spring after 13 years in power.
PSOE leader Felipe Gonzalez is rated the most highly regarded politician, leading Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar by eight-tenths of a point.
Some members of the PP attributed the loss of popularity to the "debate over regional (financing) and a press policy based on polls," the newspaper said.
